artifacts.content:
# Agent harnesses: a one-page brief

Codex, Claude Code and Hermes all take a task, run their own tools in a workspace, and hand back results and files. They differ in how they plan, which tools they expose, and what they report.

## Codex
Reasoning summaries, a small tool surface (`shell`, `apply_patch`), strong at patch-shaped edits. Reports token usage.

## Claude Code
Rich tool set (`Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Bash`, `TodoWrite`), explicit todo lists, takes more, smaller steps. Reports token usage.

## Hermes
Skill library plus memory: loads a matching skill before acting and can write new skills after. Usage accounting depends on the provider, so it may report none.

## Takeaway
Behind one Responses-compatible API (UHP), you can swap the harness by changing `metadata.harness_id` and compare them on the same task.

harness,reasoning_summary,todo_lists,skills,usage_reported,typical_tools
codex,yes,no,no,yes,"shell; apply_patch"
claude-code,no,yes,no,yes,"Read; Edit; Write; Bash; TodoWrite"
hermes,yes,no,yes,no,"terminal; read_file; write_file; skill_view"
